```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made:
- Python 3.14, per `.python-version`.
- A uv workspace of four packages under `packages/`, per the root `pyproject.toml`.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second; from the SEC full-index and daily-index directories. Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks of downloading for the full history at 3 requests/second; index row count times request rate, not yet measured. Measured by Stage 3 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk. Measured by Stage 5 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

Order follows your progression: O1, then O2, then O3, each consuming the one before. Hardening stages 6–9 follow. This diverges from the background spec, whose §7 Phase 1 builds the hardened index system (manifest, reconciliation, Azure deployment) as one phase before any measured run. Here a cheap real run comes first.

- [ ] Stage 1: Index core
      Objective: Build a filing-index table from one real closed quarter's quarterly master index and that quarter's daily indexes.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table for one quarter, read back from disk; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md, recording the result, the table's location and columns, and the measured cost
      Exit: O1 — the table holds one row per filing for the quarter, with quarterly/daily overlap deduplicated, and its row count reconciles against the source rows less duplicates; the findings file records download time, bytes, request count and row count of the real run
      Leaves out: full-history range and daily catch-up (Stage 2); source manifest and replay (Stage 6); versioned publication (Stage 6); reconciliation and withdrawal gate (Stage 7); golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Full-history range and daily catch-up
      Objective: Extend the index table over a configured quarter range, and add a daily run that ingests every daily index since its last success.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 1 table and findings
      Produces: the index table over the configured range; a daily-run command; a per-run coverage report of ingested, pending and failed source files
      Exit: O1 — the table covers the configured range; a daily run after a missed run spanning a quarter boundary ingests every listed daily index it missed; an interrupted run resumes without re-downloading completed files; the coverage report lists any gaps
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay (Stage 6); versioned publication (Stage 6); reconciliation and withdrawal gate (Stage 7); golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Submissions core
      Objective: Download the submissions named by one real daily index's rows, keeping their original bytes.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2 index table (its archive paths)
      Produces: downloaded submissions for one daily index with a per-file status list; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md, recording measured cost and the extrapolated full-range cost
      Exit: O2 — every row of the chosen daily index has its submission on disk or a recorded failure reason; the findings file records elapsed time, bytes, files per hour and the extrapolated time and volume for the configured range
      Leaves out: submissions at range scale and shared request budget (Stage 4); source manifest and replay (Stage 6); golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Submissions at range scale
      Objective: Download the submissions for a configured range resumably, sharing one SEC request budget with index runs.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 2 index table and daily-run command; Stage 3 downloader and findings
      Produces: submissions for the configured range; submissions at range scale; shared request budget across concurrent collectors; a per-quarter coverage report of downloaded, pending and failed submissions
      Exit: O2 — an interrupted download resumes without re-fetching completed files; a daily index run concurrent with the submissions download keeps the combined request rate at or under the configured target, measured over the run; the coverage report accounts for every index row in the range
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay (Stage 6); golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract each one's main document.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 4 downloaded submissions and coverage report
      Produces: extracted main documents for 10-K and 8-K filings in the range, with a list of filings that could not be extracted; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-5-findings.md, recording measured cost
      Exit: O3 — for one real quarter, every 10-K and 8-K submission on disk has its main document extracted or a recorded reason; other forms are untouched; the findings file records elapsed time, bytes and extrapolated range cost
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay (Stage 6); golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Source manifest, replay and versioned publication
      Objective: Add the source manifest and replay, and versioned publication, across index, submission and extraction outputs (background: spec §4.4–4.6).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 2, 4 and 5 outputs and their stored original bytes
      Produces: source manifest and replay; versioned publication of each index quarter through one active pointer; provenance from every output back to its source hash
      Exit: O1 — a parser-version change rebuilds the index table from stored bytes with zero SEC requests, and a crash before the pointer update leaves the prior generation readable; O2 — the manifest lists every submission with its hash and state; O3 — every extracted document traces to its submission hash and extractor version
      Leaves out: reconciliation and withdrawal gate (Stage 7); golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, record changes, and gate closed-quarter removals behind approval (background: spec §4.4).
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: Stage 6 source manifest and replay, versioned publication
      Produces: reconciliation and withdrawal gate; per-generation change records
      Exit: O1 — a changed quarterly index publishes additions and field updates with recorded before/after values; a closed-quarter replacement that removes keys stays unpublished until an approval naming its source hash; open-quarter absence removes nothing
      Leaves out: golden-fixture and fault-injection suite (Stage 8); scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Golden-fixture and fault-injection suite
      Objective: Cover the historical formats in the configured range and the failure paths with committed fixtures, running in CI with no SEC requests (background: spec §6).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stages 2–7 outputs
      Produces: golden-fixture and fault-injection suite in CI
      Exit: O1 — golden index files from every historical format in the range parse to the same table columns, and malformed, truncated and HTML inputs fail closed; O2 — injected interruptions and throttling resume without lost or duplicated submissions; O3 — fixture 10-K and 8-K submissions extract to their expected main documents; CI makes zero SEC requests
      Leaves out: scheduling, deployment and alerting (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 9: Scheduling, deployment and alerting
      Objective: Choose the platform (background: the proposed ADR) and run the daily, reconciliation and submissions work on schedule, with alerts and runbooks.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3
      Consumes: Stage 8 suite; Stages 2–7 commands
      Produces: scheduling, deployment and alerting; runbooks; a release record of image and configuration versions
      Exit: O1 — observed scheduled daily and reconciliation runs each leave a durable report; O2 — a scheduled run downloads the submissions for newly indexed rows; O3 — a scheduled run extracts the new 10-K and 8-K main documents; an injected failure raises an alert; triggers were enabled as an explicit release step
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

With every stage ticked, run derive-roadmap §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O3). Re-run the gap rubric with evidence per verdict: the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, and deferred_items entries. Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage or as a conscious deferral with a written why.
```
